svg.font-family: Inter, Segoe UI, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif
svg.text: Cross-cutting safety properties and mechanisms on top of Sub-models 1–4 — no new class tree
not a property list — its own class, sibling to Device and Component
why a full object, not a property:
a property can't carry its own test
history, id or lifecycle. One Interlock
can also govern more than one target.
Safety Instrumented Function (SIF) — Always Its Own Assembly
physically independent from the process Assembly — never mixed (Sub-model 3)
SIL is a property of the SIF Assembly as a whole, not of a single Device inside it
Interlock Paths on the Sub-model 4 State Machine
only two lockTypes exist — each one is an existing transition path, never an arbitrary jump
lockType: lock — path to Locked (continues past Inhibited)
from On, both lockTypes always route through Emergency Stopping (Category 0) —
Quick/Controlled Stopping return to Standby and are not safety-relevant paths, so an
interlock never uses them. lock reuses the inhibit path from On, then continues to Locked.
from Off, Inhibited is unreachable — an inhibit-type interlock uses the lock path's final leg
(Off → Locking → Locked) directly, rather than blocking Enabling and waiting (Sub-model 16)
the three stop states from Sub-model 4 map directly — no change needed
